clue.text: Henry in class, modest

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for Henry goes inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a social class
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry, sitting in a classroom, is described as modest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and restrained in behaviour, much as modest does.

clue.text: A solitary Channel Island has it

parts.note: Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands, between Guernsey and Sark

explanation.surface: A lonely little island in the English Channel lays claim to something.
explanation.walkthrough: HERM is a tiny Channel Island (the Channel Islands lie off the French coast but belong to the British Crown); 'has' just joins it to IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, a solitary is a recluse living alone, exactly a hermit.

clue.text: Back, form mediocre

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A complaint that a school year group is only average.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a 'form' is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-class is of inferior quality, which is what mediocre means.

clue.text: Parent so confused having to follow English language

indicators.note: having to follow places the jumbled letters after the abbreviation for English
confused says the letters of parent and so are mixed up

explanation.surface: A muddled parent has to come after an English speaker in some list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parent' reads as a family member, but it is only letters to be scrambled by 'confused'; 'having to follow' puts them after the English abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language devised by Zamenhof.

clue.text: Simple play on words used by Sherlock in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means we hear the phrase spoken rather than see it written

parts.words: play on words used by Sherlock
parts.note: a pun from Sherlock Holmes would be a Holmes pun

explanation.surface: The great detective makes a simple joke while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'Holmes pun' sounds the same as the answer, since the L in Holmes is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unsophisticated, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Fiery type, husband with Proust novel

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, signalling a fresh arrangement of the name

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered man and her husband reading a Proust novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun naming Proust's book, but it is the anagram signal. Hotspur was the nickname of Harry Percy, the hot-headed rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is a rash, hot-headed person, after Harry Percy's nickname.

clue.text: What may grow in lawn, full of energy — one found in bulrushes, too

indicators.note: full of says the lawn growth contains the energy symbol

parts.note: moss is a common weed growing in lawns
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Lawn growth teeming with life, and a baby hidden in reeds by a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too' is a link. In the Bible the infant Moses was hidden in an ark of bulrushes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus the baby Moses was placed in a basket among the bulrushes of the Nile.

clue.text: North for one passing, yet has hearts

indicators.note: hearts means the central letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A northerner passing by, who nevertheless has courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' takes the middle letters of passing, yet and has: S, E, A.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Sea is one example of a sea, hence the 'for one'.

clue.text: Demanding higher prices at college bazaar

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
a bazaar is a market

explanation.surface: Stalls at a university fair charge a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university (Oxford or Cambridge especially) while in residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods are aimed at wealthier buyers, so their sellers charge more.

clue.text: Crazy shot leads cup

indicators.note: leads places the word for shot in front of the word for cup

parts.note: a crack is an attempt, a shot at something
a pot is a sporting trophy, a cup

explanation.surface: A wild shot puts a team ahead in the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot idea or person is eccentric or mad.

clue.text: Oily sergeant major leading troops

indicators.note: leading puts the abbreviation in front of the word for troops

parts.note: an army is a body of troops

explanation.surface: A slick sergeant major heads a body of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy means unctuously ingratiating, figuratively oily in manner.

clue.text: Conqueror William's initial secret

indicators.note: initial asks for the first letter of the word William

parts.note: inner thoughts are private or secret ones

explanation.surface: A hint at a hidden fact about William the Conqueror.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at William the Conqueror, but 'Conqueror' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A conqueror is one who prevails, a winner.

clue.text: Official document left on express

indicators.note: on places the word for left after the word for express in this across entry

parts.note: to pass a remark or judgement is to express it
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A formal paper left aboard an express train.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is an official document of identity for travel.

clue.text: Fabulous bird on bow of pleasure boat here in Dublin

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the bird above what follows

parts.note: the phoenix is the mythical bird reborn from its ashes

indicators.note: bow of means the front letter, as a bow is the front of a vessel

parts.note: an ark is a boat, as Noah's was

explanation.surface: A legendary bird perched on the prow of a pleasure boat in Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenix Park is a large public park in Dublin, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Authority to keep building at airport

parts.note: control is power or authority
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: An authority being asked to preserve an airport building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep building' reads as a verb phrase, but 'keep' is the castle's stronghold and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A control tower is the airport building from which air traffic is directed.

clue.text: Dealing with one may generate a lot of interest

definitions.text: Dealing with one may generate a lot of interest

parts.words: Dealing with one may generate a lot of interest
parts.note: reads as something fascinating, but interest here is what a borrower pays on money lent at extortionate rates

explanation.surface: Something whose dealings attract much attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An unscrupulous moneylender charges very high rates of interest on loans.

clue.text: Car thief may bring girl on one condition

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the girl above the condition

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name
a rider is a condition added to an agreement

explanation.surface: A car thief might bring a girl along on one condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyrider steals a car to drive it recklessly for fun.

clue.text: Processed data, info on US drinks dispenser

indicators.note: processed signals the letters being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Computerised data and information about American soft-drink machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processed' rearranges all of DATA INFO ON US, including 'on', which looks like a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A soda fountain is a device dispensing carbonated drinks, chiefly American.

clue.text: Became aware of letter of resignation written by daughter

indicators.note: written by places the daughter abbreviation beside the letter, following it

parts.note: handing in your notice is resigning by letter

explanation.surface: Someone discovered that a daughter wrote a resignation letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticed means spotted or became aware of something.

clue.text: Finished ahead, or tied?

parts.note: done means finished
up means ahead in a contest, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A query whether a match ended with one side ahead or level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tied' looks like a drawn match but means fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: Done up means fastened or tied, as with laces or buttons.

clue.text: High-ranking army officer's role tracking money

indicators.note: tracking means following, so the role comes after the money

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
to wear a different hat is to take a different role

explanation.surface: A senior officer's job involves keeping track of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' for money is northern English slang. The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is British slang for a senior military officer, from the gold braid on the cap.

clue.text: Dye top of hair girl's swept up

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word hair
swept up in a down clue says the name reads upwards, in reverse

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Someone colours the top of a girl's hair, which has been swept upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swept up' suggests a hairstyle, but in a down clue it turns the girl's name upwards; the 's of girl's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye made from a shrub's leaves, used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Church employee attacked carrying cross

indicators.note: carrying means holding the cross inside the word for attacked

parts.note: set on means attacked
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A church worker was assaulted while bearing a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building and graveyard.

clue.text: Curious boy, very likely to succeed

parts.note: odd means curious or strange
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A strange lad tipped for success.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes a favourite whose betting odds show it is likely to win.

clue.text: Shameful offence committed by Women's Institute

indicators.note: committed by means held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A disgraceful act perpetrated by a respectable women's group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women; the letters straddle 'Women's' and 'Institute'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a moral offence or transgression.

clue.text: Hears a CD prepared for a party game

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a CD made ready for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges HEARS A CD; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a game where players mime words for others to guess.

clue.text: Strict control suggested by club worker

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: Firm discipline hinted at by a golf club employee.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron hand means harsh, firm control, as in ruling with an iron hand.

clue.text: Initially keen about keeping attractive pigeon or parrot

indicators.note: Initially takes the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A keen fancier about to keep a pretty pigeon or parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The kakapo is a large flightless nocturnal parrot of New Zealand.
